messages.text: No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week

metadata.summary: It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.
metadata.content: NFL: Pittsburgh Steelers shock Denver Broncos 27-5 after Aaron Rodgers drama dominates build-up following Mike McCarthy claims | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: Pittsburgh Steelers shock Denver Broncos 27-5 after Aaron Rodgers drama dominates build-up following Mike McCarthy claims The Pittsburgh Steelers stun the Denver Broncos 27-5 in their first game since releasing four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his remarkable comments regarding head coach Mike McCarthy; Rodgers had accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings Friday 27 November 2026 23:40, UK Image: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf scored as they beat the Denver Broncos It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers. Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game. metadata.summary: Liam Dawson insists Adil Rashid remains England's No 1 white-ball spinner - even though he has seemingly taken the Yorkshireman's place as first-choice pick in ODIs.
metadata.content: England T20s in Australia: Liam Dawson says Adil Rashid still No 1 spinner as tourists target series victory in Sydney | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England T20s in Australia: Liam Dawson says Adil Rashid still No 1 spinner as tourists target series victory in Sydney Liam Dawson has been preferred to Adil Rashid in ODIs of late but spinners play together in T20s, helping England into a 2-1 series lead over Australia with two matches left; Dawson hails two more spinners in James Coles and Rehan Ahmed ahead of Sunday's fixture in Sydney (8.15am UK) Saturday 28 November 2026 07:28, UK Image: Liam Dawson (left) and Adil Rashid (right) are key players for England in T20 international cricket Liam Dawson insists Adil Rashid remains England's No 1 white-ball spinner - even though he has seemingly taken the Yorkshireman's place as first-choice pick in ODIs. Stalwart Rashid, 38, has been left out of England's last six 50-over encounters - three in Pakistan and then three in Australia - with Dawson the frontline slow bowler for those games. The duo form a potent pairing in T20 internationals, though, and bowled economically - and in Dawson's case prolifically, as he took 3-16 from three overs - in Brisbane on Friday as England took a 2-1 lead over Australia in the five-match series. metadata.summary: Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.
metadata.content: Players Championship Finals: Gerwyn Price out in first round as Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen progress at Minehead | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Players Championship Finals: Gerwyn Price out in first round as Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen progress at Minehead Report as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman all knocked out in first round at Players Championship Finals; watch the World Darts Championship at London's Alexandra Palace, live on Sky Sports from December 11-January 3 Noah Langford Sports Journalist Friday 27 November 2026 23:46, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastian Bialecki beats Gerwyn Price to advance in the Players Championship Finals! Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead. Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline. Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history. messages.text: 'A bit strange' - Leclerc seeking outlier to catch Mercedes in Qatar

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions.
metadata.content: Charles Leclerc seeking outlier as Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull try to catch Mercedes at Qatar Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Charles Leclerc seeking outlier as Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull try to catch Mercedes at Qatar Grand Prix Mercedes dominated Friday's practice sessions at the Qatar Grand Prix and Charles Leclerc suggested Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull are missing something; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead of Qualifying at 6pm on Saturday live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 27 November 2026 20:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Qatar Grand Prix Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions. Mercedes were nearly half a second quicker than the rest of the field at the Lusail International Circuit as Antonelli topped both sessions from Russell. Their four-tenths advantage over closest challenger Lando Norris in second practice could have been even greater, with neither Antonelli nor Russell completing a full low-fuel lap on the soft tyres. It was an ominous sign for the rest of the field ahead of Saturday's qualifying, which gets under way at 6pm, with coverage live on Sky Sports F1 from 5.15pm.
